key_insight: SHARE is a human-AI co-learning framework that combines expert review with model reasoning to improve scalable labeling of disease activity from EHR notes.
clinical_relevance: It may help produce more accurate and reproducible phenotyping for rheumatoid arthritis and other complex outcomes to support real-world evidence generation.
method: Experts and an AI agent labeled notes with the same guideline, then adjudicated disagreements into co-produced labels
Tested a budget-tiered setup using GPT-5 Nano for extraction and o4-mini for reasoning, benchmarked against a higher-effort GPT-5.4 configuration
evidence_signal: On 686 co-produced reference notes, the final agent improved MAE from 0.406 to 0.291, agreed with ambiguity flags at 92.1%, and the budget-tiered setup cut estimated cost by 69% and compute time by 70% while matching GPT-5.4 performance.
watch_item: Performance was demonstrated in rheumatoid arthritis EHR data, so generalization to other diseases, sites, or documentation styles still needs validation.
paper_title: A framework for human-artificial intelligence co-learning for disease activity labeling using electronic health records
